long_biography.plain_text:
Alca's rise as one of Croatia's leading distributors followed a severe early test for Michael Markota. His father Žarko had founded the trading business between East and West, but the Yugoslav wars broke its import-export model apart. After the conflict, Markota rebuilt its position around reliable delivery for consumer brands, including an early distribution relationship with Gillette.

Markota turned that recovery into a broader logistics platform serving south-eastern Europe. The company combined sales, warehousing, delivery and financial-risk management, while reinvesting profits in regional infrastructure. As supervisory-board chairman, he has described investments in people, digital processes and long-term partnerships as the decisions that modernised Alca. He also regards periods of expansion that outran internal systems as a lesson in favour of sustainable growth.
